title: Cold rebuild: Fragment a datagram
summary: Rebuild Fragment a datagram from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Fragment a datagram** in *UDP, ICMP and MTU*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: What MSS does each link MTU allow (IPv4 and TCP headers are 20 bytes each)?
steps.explain: 1280 is also the minimum MTU every IPv6 link must support.

steps.title: Rebuild Fragment a datagram cold
prompt: Write `List<(int Offset, int Length, bool More)> Fragment(int payload, int mtu)` splitting an IP payload of `payload` bytes for a link MTU (20-byte IP header per fragment).
Each fragment carries at most `(mtu - 20)` rounded **down to a multiple of 8** bytes; `Offset` is in 8-byte units; `More` is true on all but the last.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
List<(int Offset, int Length, bool More)> Fragment(int payload, int mtu)
